articles.title: Allison Ellsworth began mixing a homemade soda in her Texas kitchen, then took it from farmers’ markets to Shark Tank; 10 years later PepsiCo acquired Poppi in a $1.95 billion deal
articles.summary: A homemade drink prepared in a Texas home's kitchen about a decade ago became a beverage business worth nearly $2 billion.
articles.body: A homemade drink prepared in a Texas home's kitchen about a decade ago became a beverage business worth nearly $2 billion. Allison Ellsworth, was experimenting with fruit, apple cider vinegar and soda water to address her personal digestive concerns. The recipe for her health went on to become Poppi, a business co-founded with her husband, Stephen. In 2025, PepsiCo acquired the company in a $1.95 billion deal.The business had modest beginnings. Before Poppi became a recognised soda brand, Ellsworth was selling her drink at farmers’ markets, trying to convince customers to taste something unfamiliar. But her appearance on the television programme Shark Tank while nine months pregnant secured an investment that helped the business move forward.The company subsequently built its audience through social media and expanded into major American retail chains. According to Fortune magazine, Poppi recorded annual revenue exceeding $500 million in 2024 and was available at more than 120 retailers. Its acquisition by PepsiCo followed years of expansion. The company has also faced questions over its health-related marketing claims.Speaking on Adam Mendler's Thirty Minute Mentors podcast, Ellsworth talked about the decisions that shaped Poppi, including her early attempts to attract customers, her experience with TikTok and the difficulties of managing a business growing faster than she had expected.Why Allison Ellsworth started making her own drinkEllsworth's interest in creating a beverage developed after she began experiencing digestive problems and persistent tiredness. She tried drinking apple cider vinegar but found its taste unpleasant. This prompted her to experiment with different ingredients until she developed something she preferred drinking.Her initial intention was not to establish a major beverage company. During the podcast interview, she explained that she wanted to share a product she had created for herself.However, turning that personal experiment into something customers would purchase proved challenging. At farmers’ markets, Ellsworth encountered people who struggled to understand what made her drink different from other beverages.Their responses were not always encouraging. Rather than receiving immediate enthusiasm, she often found herself explaining the product repeatedly. Those conversations became an early opportunity to understand how customers viewed the drink.The business gained wider attention in 2018 when Ellsworth appeared on Shark Tank. On the show, investor Rohan Oza agreed to invest $400,000. Ellsworth was nine months pregnant during her appearance and, according to her podcast account, she gave birth 10 days later.How TikTok helped Poppi reach more customersPoppi's official launch came in March 2020, just as the Covid-19 pandemic was beginning. The timing created a difficult environment for introducing a consumer brand, prompting Ellsworth to explore other ways of reaching people.She turned to TikTok, where she began posting videos without a dedicated production team or formal social media training. Some featured recipes and dancing, while others focused on her experiences as a founder.Ellsworth acknowledged that she initially felt uncomfortable appearing in these videos. Nevertheless, the response helped her identify which parts of her story interested viewers.A particularly successful post involved her explaining how the drink originated in her kitchen and eventually reached Shark Tank. She told Mendler that the video attracted widespread attention and generated $100,000 in sales while she was asleep.Following that experience, Poppi continued investing in digital marketing and direct communication with consumers. Its promotional activities extended beyond conventional beverage advertising to include influencers, events and brand collaborations.From supermarket shelves to PepsiCo acquisitionAs Poppi's popularity increased, the company expanded its retail presence and introduced a range of flavours. Poppi offered 16 flavours and had attracted celebrity investors, including Olivia Munn, Post Malone, Alix Earle and Nicole Scherzinger.According to Ellsworth, approximately 250 employees were hired over four years. Having initially handled several responsibilities herself, she eventually brought in experienced professionals to manage areas where she lacked expertise.Customer feedback also influenced product decisions. Ellsworth recalled that Poppi's root beer flavour had struggled commercially for two years. After receiving complaints about its taste and packaging, the company revised both and openly discussed the criticism on social media. She said the updated product subsequently became one of its stronger sellers.By 2024, Poppi's annual revenue had crossed $500 million, according to figures reported by Fortune. The following year, PepsiCo completed its acquisition of the company for $1.95 billion, a figure that included an estimated $300 million in cash tax benefits.However, the company's expansion was not without controversy. Fortune reported that Poppi agreed to an $8.9 million settlement following a class action lawsuit challenging its marketing claims about digestive health. The company maintained that the settlement did not amount to an admission of wrongdoing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2016, Barack Obama faced a patchwork of unprotected California desert; he created three monuments, and nearly 2 million acres gained protection
articles.summary: In 2016, President Obama designated three national monuments in Southern California, safeguarding nearly 1.8 million acres of desert land. Discover the significance of Mojave Trails, Sand to Snow, and Castle Mountains and their impact on wildlife and conservation.
articles.body: President Barack Obama designated three national monuments in Southern California on February 12, 2016, which placed nearly 1.8 million acres of federal land under national monument protection. The three sites were Mojave Trails, Sand to Snow and Castle Mountains, which are a group of desert landscapes that also connected several areas that were already protected as national parks, preserves and wilderness. The U.S. Department of the Interior said the designations followed decades of local input and conservation efforts.Mojave Trails covered 1.6 million acresThe largest designation was Mojave Trails National Monument, which covers about 1.6 million acres in the eastern Mojave Desert, and its boundaries included rugged mountain ranges, ancient lava flows, sand dunes and desert valleys. The area also contained historic Native American trading routes, World War II-era military training sites and the longest remaining undeveloped stretch of Route 66.More than 350,000 acres within Mojave Trails had already been designated as wilderness by Congress, and Obama’s proclamation placed the wider landscape under the national monument designation and linked it with other protected areas in the region. The Mojave Trails proclamation specifically identified lava flows, volcanic features, caves, sand dunes, mountains, and other geological formations as resources to be protected. The monument included Amboy Crater and the Pisgah Volcano area, where lava tubes form one of Southern California’s highest concentrations of caves.Sand to Snow ran from desert floor to alpine mountainSand to Snow National Monument stretches from the Sonoran Desert floor toward San Gorgonio Mountain, which is the highest peak in Southern California, across an elevation range of nearly 10,000 feet. The monument contained more than 100,000 acres of wilderness that Congress had already designated, and also included about 30 miles of the Pacific Crest Trail, desert oases and archaeological sites, including an estimated 1,700 Native American petroglyphs. Federal officials identified more than 240 bird species and 12 threatened or endangered wildlife species in the area.Obama’s proclamation described the area as a connection between the San Bernardino National Forest and Joshua Tree National Park, and its varied terrain included desert scrub, riparian areas, woodlands, chaparral and alpine forests. Wildlife recorded in the region included bighorn sheep, mountain lions, black bears, bobcats, and several federally listed species.Castle Mountains filled another gapThe smallest of the three was Castle Mountains National Monument, which covers approximately 20,920 acres, sits next to Mojave National Preserve and contains Joshua tree forests, desert grasslands, mountain habitat, and archaeological sites. The area also includes the historic Hart mining site and the Castle Mountains themselves, with Hart Peak rising to 5,543 feet, and the proclamation identified the area as an important connection for wildlife and water between the New York and Piute Mountains. Desert bighorn sheep, golden eagles, bats and desert tortoises are among the wildlife found there.The three monuments were designed to connect protected landThe three designations covered roughly 1.775 million acres, which federal officials rounded to nearly 1.8 million, and the administration said that the new monuments would connect existing protected areas, including Joshua Tree National Park, Mojave National Preserve and 15 congressionally designated wilderness areas. The designations were made under the Antiquities Act, which gives presidents authority to establish national monuments on federal land to protect objects of historic or scientific interest. Obama had used the law repeatedly during his presidency, but the California desert action was one of his largest single conservation designations.Federal officials said that activities including hiking, camping, hunting, horseback riding, photography and other outdoor uses would continue under monument management rules. The February 2016 designations instead added another layer of federal protection across a landscape that already contained several different categories of protected public land.You use AI every day. articles.title: A man bought a Hyundai Eon in 2016 but never got its RC or invoice; Punjab consumer commission ordered the company and dealer to provide documents, pay Rs 22,500
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Punjab state consumer commission has dismissed Hyundai’s appeal and upheld an order directing the company and its dealer to provide a buyer
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Punjab state consumer commission has dismissed Hyundai’s appeal and upheld an order directing the company and its dealer to provide a buyer with the vehicle’s invoice and registration certificate (RC), and pay Rs 22,500 towards compensation along with litigation costs. The commission held that Hyundai could not evade responsibility for its dealer’s failure to provide the required documents.The commission passed the order on October 6, 2026, after finding no merit in Hyundai’s contention that it was not responsible for the dealer’s conduct.New Hyundai Eon without invoiceAccording to the commission order, Amandeep Singh, the complainant, bought a white Hyundai Eon Era+B from Ahuja Automobiles, an authorised Hyundai dealer in Amritsar, on June 15, 2016. He paid Rs 1,04,500 as a down payment, while the remaining Rs 2.6 lakh was financed through ICICI Bank, which he was to repay in monthly instalments of Rs 5,525.The dealer issued receipts for the down payment and a delivery challan but did not give him the car’s invoice. The complainant was allegedly told that, because the purchase was financed, the invoice would be provided through the bank after the formalities were completed. He also did not receive the registration certificate.The complainant alleged that he made repeated requests to the dealer and other parties, including through telephone calls and personal visits, but did not get the documents. He approached the consumer commission, seeking the invoice and registration certificate or a refund, along with compensation for the harassment and litigation costs.However, Hyundai argued that the dispute concerned the dealer and the bank, not the manufacturer. It said its relationship with dealers was on a principal-to-principal basis and that preparing the registration documents and issuing the invoice were not its responsibilities. ICICI Bank also said it had provided the vehicle loan and was not responsible for registration formalities.The district consumer commission in Tarn Taran, ruled in the complainant’s favour on September 15, 2022, directing the dealer and Hyundai to provide the documents and pay Rs 15,000 as compensation and Rs 7,500 towards litigation expenses.Hyundai then challenged that order before the state commission.Commission's findingThe bench of presiding judicial member Harinderpal Singh Mahal and member Kiran Sibal rejected the Hyundai’s argument that it could not be held responsible for the dealer’s conduct.The commission said that the dealer sold vehicles manufactured by Hyundai and was authorised by the company to sell them to consumers. It held that a manufacturer could not avoid responsibility merely by arguing that it had no direct contractual relationship with the retail buyer.“A manufacturer cannot be escaped its liability merely by contending that it is only the manufacturer and has nothing to do with the retail sale of the goods,” the commission observed.It then said that the Hyundai Motors India were expected to remain vigilant about how their authorised dealers dealt with customers and to take corrective action when complaints of improper or deficient service arose.The commission further noted that the buyer had paid for the vehicle and continued to repay the loan despite not receiving the documents needed to establish ownership. It found no merit in Hyundai’s argument that it had no responsibility for the dealer’s actions.“We do not find any merit in the pleas taken by the appellant/opposite party No.2 that they have nothing to do with the selling of the cars by the dealers, rather they are fully responsible for the acts and conducts of the dealers,” the commission said.What did the commission order?In its October 6, 2026, order, the Punjab State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission dismissed Hyundai’s appeal and upheld the District Consumer Commission’s directions.The order requires the dealer and Hyundai to:Provide the car’s registration certificate and invoice to the buyer.Pay Rs 15,000 as compensation for harassment and mental agony.Pay Rs 7,500 towards litigation expenses.The commission also directed that Rs 16,600 deposited by Hyundai when filing the appeal, along with any interest accrued on it, be remitted to the complainant after 45 days from the sending of certified copies of the order, in accordance with law.The ruling reinforces that a vehicle manufacturer cannot automatically distance itself from complaints about an authorised dealer’s conduct simply because the retail sale took place through the dealer. Hyundai’s appeal was dismissed, leaving the original consumer commission’s directions in place.

articles.title: Keke Palmer is bringing her KeyTV experience to UCLA; three upcoming sessions will focus on artistic identity, creative power and community
articles.summary: Keke Palmer’s five-year collaboration with the University of California, Los Angeles School of Theater, Film and Television is moving into its first
articles.body: Keke Palmer’s five-year collaboration with the University of California, Los Angeles School of Theater, Film and Television is moving into its first academic-year programme, with three sessions planned for students during 2026–27. The Emmy-winning actor, producer and entrepreneur, Lauren Palmer, known professionally as Keke Palmer, has been named the University of California, Los Angeles School of Theatre, Film and Television’s artist in residence for the 2026–27 academic year. UCLA TFT’s August 18 announcement outlines three quarterly sessions under the title “Know Yourself, Own Yourself, Free Yourself to Build New Frameworks for Change”. The sessions will explore artistic identity, creative ownership and community, and will take place at Freud Playhouse on campus. Dean Celine Parreñas Shimizu will curate and moderate the sessions, which are open to TFT students. The residency forms part of a five-year partnership with Palmer’s digital media network, KeyTV, announced by UCLA in June 2026.Keke Palmer’s UCLA residency: Three sessions on creative identity, ownership and communityUCLA TFT’s August announcement sets out three quarterly sessions for the 2026–27 academic year under the title Know Yourself, Own Yourself, Free Yourself to Build New Frameworks for Change. The sessions will be held at Freud Playhouse on campus and are open to TFT students. Dean Celine Parreñas Shimizu will curate the programme and moderate the sessions, which will include assigned readings. The fall 2026 session, “Your Voice. Our Story.”, will examine self-perception, public perception and artistic voice. The winter 2027 session, “Owning Your Creative Power”, will focus on Palmer’s experience building KeyTV and responding to gaps in the entertainment industry. The spring 2027 session, “The Modern Multi-Hyphenate: Freedom Through Community”, will explore her work across acting, producing, entrepreneurship, media and authorship, with an emphasis on creative independence and community. UCLA’s June 11 announcement describes KeyTV as the distribution platform for selected student projects, connecting work developed through the partnership with audiences beyond the classroom. The collaboration brings together UCLA’s production training and Palmer’s experience in entertainment and digital media.KeyTV and UCLA student content: How the partnership plans to distribute projectsUCLA’s June 11 announcement says Palmer co-founded KeyTV in 2021 and that the network launched in November 2022. The release reported that KeyTV had produced 29 projects since its launch and described its productions as BIPOC-creator-led. UCLA’s June 11 announcement says KeyTV plans to distribute at least three student projects each year, subject to quality review. The arrangement is intended to expose students to aspects of the media business beyond production, including packaging, marketing and digital audience engagement.What the Keke Palmer-UCLA partnership does not yet specifyAlthough the announcement outlines the programme’s structure and distribution plans, it leaves several practical questions unanswered. It does not explain how students will be selected for the studio course, whether participation will be open to students across different majors, or what application deadlines and academic-credit requirements will apply. The announcement describes the studio course as fully sponsored but does not identify the source of its funding. It also does not specify who will own the completed projects, what rights KeyTV will receive, or whether students will be paid if their work is distributed. The quality-review process for projects considered for KeyTV distribution is another detail that remains unspecified.The June announcement also outlines a fully sponsored studio course planned for the 2027–28 academic year. With Palmer mentoring students, the course is expected to support projects including video podcasts, television pilots, music videos and musical or dance-theatre productions. KeyTV is intended to provide a distribution route for selected work produced through the collaboration. These questions matter because the collaboration combines university instruction with the distribution of creative work through an external media platform. The programme’s eventual value to students will depend not only on access to mentorship and production experience but also on how project selection, ownership and distribution are handled.The programme will unfold in stages. Quarterly workshops are scheduled for the 2026-27 academic year, while the studio course is due to begin in 2027-28. The announcement does not provide detailed dates for individual workshops or explain when students can apply for the course. Reporting by The Hollywood Reporter has also described the plan as involving mentorship and the production of selected student projects under Palmer’s KeyTV banner. The five-year term gives UCLA and KeyTV time to develop the collaboration across multiple academic years, although the programme’s outcomes will become clearer as the workshops and studio course get underway.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump calls Ukraine’s renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries ‘a disgrace’
articles.summary: US president says Zelenskyy ‘more difficult ​to deal with ​than Putin’ after ‘energy ceasefire’ collapses
articles.body:
Donald Trump has called Ukraine's renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries "a disgrace" and criticised Volodymyr ⁠Zelenskyy after an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine failed to take hold.

Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries ⁠after Zelenskyy said Kyiv was abandoning a ceasefire unilaterally declared by Trump on Sunday, having briefly halted its attacks to demonstrate its readiness for peace talks. Russia had continued its strikes on Ukrainian power plants.

In an interview with Newsmax aired on Thursday, the US president said: "All he's doing is making the world oil price higher. Well, I think that's a disgrace.

"There are a lot ‌of targets you can ‌hit, but when you shoot at diesel refineries where you make, you know, ‌diesel oil, and we need that, and the world needs that, then he's not doing a good service for the world."

Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since Trump announced an easing sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel on to global markets.

Zelenskyy criticised the agreement, which was widely interpreted as an attempt to curb high fuel prices before the US midterm elections, saying it would allow Russia to press on with its full-scale invasion of Ukraine that began more than four and a half years ago. US efforts under Trump to end the war have made no progress.

Trump repeated to Newsmax his views of the two leaders involved in the conflict. "I'm not a big fan of Zelenskyy," Trump said. "I think they actually both would like to see it ⁠end, but I think I find Zelenskyy to be more difficult ​to deal with ​than Putin."

Arriving in Brussels to meet EU leaders on Friday, Zelenskyy did not comment on Trump's latest remarks. He said he was "so thankful that we have such huge support from the EU" and its leaders, whom he described as "real leaders".

He went on to say that Ukraine wanted to end the war as quickly as possible, but "we don't see now signals from [the] Russian side that they are ready for this".

Kyiv's relationship with Washington was strained further this week when Ukraine said Starlink services had been restricted , in effect hobbling Ukrainian drone strike missions and crucial air defences with a flick of the switch.

During a visit to London this week, the Ukrainian president said the sudden restriction of Starlink had left him feeling personally betrayed by Trump and lamented losing a partner.

The British defence secretary, Wes Streeting, said on Thursday that his US counterpart, Pete Hegseth, had assured him in a face-to-face meeting that the vital satellite communications system had been restored. In an interview with the BBC, he said it was unclear what had caused the disruption, but added: "This is not the first time we've seen a falling out between Washington and Kyiv."

Amid growing doubts about long-term US commitment to Ukraine, European leaders declared their support for Zelenskyy.

Standing alongside the Ukrainian leader in Brussels, the European Council president, António Costa, said Ukraine could "count on us not only to support you in war" but also in the path to negotiating EU membership.

The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said the EU had supported Trump's energy ceasefire, "but we have seen that Russia did not respect it, not a single minute" and instead had escalated its attacks. She said the EU intended to increase pressure on Russia, promising a 22nd round of sanctions, adding: "We will not lift any sanctions unless Russia stops the war."

The promise of further European sanctions against Russia comes weeks after the EU lifted sanctions against two prominent Russian oligarchs at the request of France and Luxembourg.

After meeting Zelenskyy, the French president, Emmanuel Macron, said it was "crucial" that Ukraine received "all the means necessary to protect itself".

The Polish prime minister, Donald Tusk, posted online: "I can reassure you, dear Ukrainian friends and President Zelenskyy: YOU ARE NOT ALONE."

As Zelenskyy met Macron in Brussels, he said that the Kremlin had "launched yet another vile drone strike on Ukrainian energy infrastructure" in the city of Lutsk, which caused blackouts.

The Kremlin, meanwhile, accused Ukraine of derailing US peace efforts by resuming its strikes on refineries.

articles.title: Action needed to save water, minister tells MPs
articles.summary: Severe drought was declared across parts of southern England after months of low rainfall.
articles.body:
The government has warned action is needed to prevent water shortages becoming "the norm" after severe drought was declared across parts of southern England.

Water and flooding minister Emma Hardy told MPs current drought conditions were "something we have not experienced for decades" and urged people to "think about ways to use water wisely over the coming weeks".

Severe drought was declared across parts of southern England on Thursday after months of low rainfall, with around 50 million people now impacted.

Parts of Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex and West Sussex are all affected by the move announced by the Environment Agency.

The government said supplies would not be interrupted but declaring severe drought would ensure "proactive steps are taken to safeguard water before any disruption occurs".

Speaking in the House of Commons, Hardy said the measures were down to "exceptionally low rainfall" and depleted reservoir levels.

How we got to severe drought and what is next

Severe drought declared and hosepipe bans in force - is your area affected?

Drought permit issued in bid to secure supply

The minister noted Yorkshire also moved into drought status last week.

"That means over 80% of England is now in drought, affecting around 50 million people," she said.

"The South East and South West, in particular, have experienced their driest April to September in over a century.

"While the record-breaking heat and lack of rainfall have put our water resources under immense this year, we must take action now to prevent this situation becoming the norm."

Robbie Moore, shadow minister for environment, food and rural affairs, accused the government of being "slow to react" to the conditions.

"This is the third drought in five years, it should not have caught the government off guard," he told MPs.

Hardy insisted "we know that this the new normal when it comes to our weather", adding: "This is exactly why we are preparing for it."

The latest figures for Wimbleball Reservoir on Exmoor show it is at 14.9% capacity, while Ardingly in West Sussex is 19.4% full. Other major reservoirs are also low, including Roadford in Devon at 36.8%, Burrator at 33.6%, Colliford in Cornwall at 35% and Stithians at 21.9%.

Wimbleball serves about 300,000 properties across east Devon, north Devon, Somerset, west Dorset and west Somerset, while Ardingly Reservoir supplies 280,000.

As part of the severe drought conditions, water companies have been asked to conduct daily monitoring of these reservoir levels along with tougher monitoring of water quality.

The Environment Agency was also expected to increase compliance checks on businesses withdrawing water from natural sources to ensure they only take permitted quantities.

It said "small changes" including taking shorter showers, fixing leaks and turning off taps while brushing teeth could "make a real difference".

"These aren't token gestures," the agency said.

"They cut the amount of water we need to take from rivers and groundwater, protecting supplies for people and leaving more for wildlife, wetlands and the natural systems we all depend on."

The Environment Agency said further dry weather was expected for the rest of October: "The usual seasonal rainfall has yet to arrive, and 82% of England remains in drought."

In some areas, 120% of the expected rainfall was needed for the next six months or "drought conditions will continue and could worsen", it said.

Severe drought is the most serious level, and was declared "when evidence shows drought is causing, or will soon cause, serious harm, and that emergency action is needed to protect people, water supplies, the environment, farming, infrastructure or other critical services".

articles.title: An Australian dairy farmer has worked in Mirboo North for 43 years; now a 345-km power cable plans a 4-hectare easement across his 180-hectare farm and offers $8,000 per km annually for 25 years
articles.summary: For 43 years, Paul Peluso has built his life around the rhythms of dairy farming in Mirboo North, Victoria.
articles.body: For 43 years, Paul Peluso has built his life around the rhythms of dairy farming in Mirboo North, Victoria. Moving cattle between paddocks, managing pastures and keeping the milking operation running are routines shaped by years of working the same land. Now, a major electricity transmission project threatens to disrupt that carefully established system, leaving the farmer weighing the promise of compensation against the potential cost to his livelihood, states an online report by Head Topics. Scroll down to read the details.A power line through working farmlandAccording to the online report, Peluso’s farm lies along the proposed route of Marinus Link, a 345-kilometre electricity and communications connection linking Tasmania with Victoria. The project will run beneath Bass Strait before continuing underground through Gippsland to the Latrobe Valley, adds the report.The report adds that for Peluso, the immediate concern is a proposed four-hectare easement across his 180-hectare property. Although the cables will be buried, construction will require trenching and access to the land over a period that could extend across six years. The route also cuts across tracks used to move cattle between paddocks and the milking sheds. Peluso fears that construction, changes to water movement and possible soil disturbance could affect pasture growth and make daily farm operations more difficult.Compensation versus long-term lossesIf we go by the report by Head Topics, the proposed arrangement includes an annual payment of $8,000 per kilometre for 25 years, alongside compensation for the construction period. Peluso believes the initial construction payment falls well short of the losses he anticipates from disruption to his business.The report also mentions that his niece, Emma Germano, a former Victorian Farmers Federation president, is helping him negotiate the terms. She is concerned that the easement could also affect the property's resale value, with prospective buyers potentially reluctant to take on a farm facing uncertain construction impacts and long-term restrictions.A request to shift the easement towards a rear boundary fence to reduce interference with cattle loading was rejected, adding to the family's concerns about how the project will affect the property.A national energy project with local consequencesFor the uninitiated, Marinus Link is designed to strengthen electricity sharing between Tasmania and Victoria. Its first stage will provide 750 megawatts of capacity, enough to supply approximately 750,000 homes. Tasmania's hydroelectric generation could help meet Victorian demand, while surplus solar and wind power from Victoria could flow in the opposite direction.The project involves 255 kilometres of undersea cable and 90 kilometres of underground cable in Victoria. The first stage is scheduled for completion in 2030, followed by a second stage in 2033. The combined cost of the two stages was estimated at $7.57 billion by the Australian Energy Market Operator in August last year.Also, energy analysts argue that the connection will become increasingly important as coal-fired power stations close and electricity demand rises. Better links between the states could help manage supply and reduce pressure on wholesale prices.Finding a balance between progress and livelihoodsNot everyone is convinced that the benefits justify every local cost. Critics point to the rapid expansion of battery storage across Australia and question some of the assumptions behind major transmission investments. Marinus Link says it has engaged with landholders since 2019 and aims to negotiate access respectfully, with compulsory acquisition considered only when necessary. The time required on individual properties will depend on factors including weather, engineering requirements and ground conditions.Image Courtesy: istock and Head TopicsYou use AI every day. articles.title: In 1993, Micky Thornton began digging a backyard pool in Covington, Tennessee; nearly three decades later, it had grown into a 500,000-gallon water playground using 40,000 pounds of rebar and 320 yards of gunite
articles.summary: Most people who dream of a backyard pool imagine a simple rectangle with a diving board and a few lounge chairs.
articles.body: Most people who dream of a backyard pool imagine a simple rectangle with a diving board and a few lounge chairs. Micky Thornton imagined something far bigger. When he moved to Covington, Tennessee, in 1992, he wanted a place where his family could swim, but he also carried an idea from childhood that refused to stay small. By the time work began on Labor Day in 1993, Thornton was preparing to create a pond-sized water playground rather than an ordinary swimming pool.Nearly three decades later, that project had become a remarkable 500,000-gallon backyard pool built with 320 yards of gunite and 40,000 pounds of steel rebar. It includes rock-lined waterfalls, sprayers and a filtration system Thornton designed himself. According to WGN-TV and TurnTo23, the pool began as a family project but eventually became a destination for parties, weddings, reunions and baptisms. Read more Thornton and how he mde his childhood dream come true here:A childhood idea became a lifelong projectAs per the reports, Thornton said the idea first came to him when he was about nine or ten years old. He did not want a pool where swimmers felt confined to a small box. Instead, he wanted a large and deep space where people could swim freely, dive and enjoy the water without feeling restricted.When he moved to Covington at the age of 38, the dream returned with greater urgency. He was 39 when he started digging in 1993 and later explained that he felt it was time to begin if he ever wanted to build something on that scale. The initial excavation went more than 20 feet deep and was first lined with a polyethylene mat, according to WGN-TV.His wife, Jane Thornton, had only one major request: the pool should not sit beside the house. Micky wanted to use the pasture land that sloped downhill, while Jane believed he could find a way to make it work. That conversation led to a layout that allowed the pool to spread across the property rather than crowd the family home, as per the reports.Built with steel, concrete and patienceThe pool’s construction was never a single-season job. Thornton began with a basic excavation and liner, then kept improving the space as the years passed. In 1998 and 1999, the family replaced the rubber liner and added a waterfall along with much of the rock decoration. Those features lasted about 15 years before the pool received another major update in 2013.The finished structure relies on serious engineering materials. It uses 320 yards of gunite, a cement-and-sand mixture applied under pressure and often used for tunnels and structural repairs, along with 40,000 pounds of steel rebar. Those materials gave the pool the strength and shape needed to hold an estimated 500,000 gallons of water.Thornton also had to solve the practical challenge of keeping that much water clean. Because the pool was far larger than a standard residential design, he built his own filtration system from the beginning. WGN-TV reported that he created a system that was more effective and efficient than conventional options, allowing the unusual backyard pool to remain usable for large groups.A backyard that became a community spaceAlthough the pool was originally intended for Thornton’s family, it quickly attracted friends, neighbours and visitors. The Thorntons initially allowed people to swim free of charge, but so many guests offered to pay that the couple eventually settled on a reasonable fixed donation.Over time, the pool became the setting for children’s soccer-team gatherings, birthday parties, family reunions, weddings and other large outings. The Thorntons began accepting reservations through their Facebook page, turning their private backyard into a place where families could celebrate major moments together.The pool has also hosted some unexpected visitors. Jane Thornton recalled that the Japanese National baseball team asked to spend an afternoon there. She expected about 25 people, but 50 arrived, giving the backyard pool an international moment few homeowners could have predicted.Baptisms gave the pool deeper meaningBeyond the parties and swimming, the pool became a spiritual space for many people. Thornton said that more than 400 people from different churches have been baptized in its waters. He described that as something he found meaningful, even though he regretted never keeping an exact count of every baptism, as per WGN-TV.That detail changes the way the pool should be understood. It is not merely an oversized construction project or an unusual piece of backyard engineering. For many visitors, it became a place of celebration, community and personal milestones, from childhood birthdays to weddings and religious ceremonies.Rev. Keith King, Pastor of Worship even praised the Thornton family for helping in over 400 baptisms in their pool. Rev. Keith King said in an article on St. Luke's Methodist Church's website, "Their pool has truly been a dream come true and has been a huge blessing to others... Each of us has a passion, a dream. The Thornton family has shown that when you work to make a dream come true, and share that dream with others, you find great joy. When you share your passion with others you become a blessing."A reminder that big dreams take timeThornton’s pool stands out because it was built gradually, with vision and persistence rather than a rushed timetable. What began as a deep hole in a Tennessee pasture evolved over decades into a 500,000-gallon water playground with waterfalls, rock features, sprayers and space for hundreds of guests.His story is a reminder that ambitious ideas do not always need to be completed immediately. Sometimes they need time, repeated improvements and the willingness to keep working long after the initial excitement fades. Thornton started with a childhood wish for room to swim and ended up creating one of the most extraordinary backyard pools ever built.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2007, Dog Whisperer César Millan moved his Dog Psychology Center to a 43-acre California ranch; the facility works with dogs that could otherwise face euthanasia
articles.summary: Explore César Millan's Dog Psychology Center in Santa Clarita, where abandoned and at-risk dogs are rehabilitated and saved from euthanasia. Learn about the facility's history, training techniques, and anti-euthanasia mission.
articles.body: The Santa Clarita Valley lies north of Los Angeles. One of the properties there is the Dog Psychology Center, the working base of Cesar Millan, a dog behavior specialist who hosted Dog Whisperer on the National Geographic Channel and later fronted other television series. The center has served as a location in his shows. Millan’s own website also describes owner-training programs held at the site, which are separate from the rehabilitation work done with dogs. The rehabilitation of dogs that owners and shelters have trouble placing and that might otherwise be euthanized is, according to Millan, the purpose of the center. The center grew out of an earlier facility in Los Angeles, which was relocated north to Santa Clarita. The foundation’s own pages and a small number of secondary sources are the main record of that history.The 1998 South Central Los Angeles center and the reported move to Santa ClaritaThe GuideStar profile of the Cesar Millan Foundation states that Millan established his Dog Psychology Center in South Central Los Angeles in 1998, and Newsmakers, a biographical reference, gives the same year. The sources reviewed do not provide any information about the acquisition of the Santa Clarita property. BroadwayWorld described César Millán’s first Dog Psychology Center as a two-acre facility in South Los Angeles that housed 30 to 40 dogs considered “un-adoptable” and abandoned. It also mentions that the move to the Santa Clarita Valley was made in order to expand the facility and update its facilities.The sources reviewed date the move to 2007 or 2009 and none of them settles the question. A 2007 San Fernando Valley Business Journal report described Millan as still considering Santa Clarita at that time, and noted that the Santa Clarita Valley Film Office had counted 387 production days in the first six months of 2006.The 43-acre site and the reported size of its packCesar Millan’s official website describes the Dog Psychology Center in Santa Clarita as a 43-acre facility with roads and walking trails, a swimming pool, spacious kennels, and farm animals. Pet Life Radio adds that the center has air-conditioned kennels, a sheep herding area and an obstacle course. Newsmakers describes the site as a 40-acre compound, slightly smaller than the 43 acres on Millan’s website.Newsmakers, a biographical reference, notes that Millan keeps a revolving pack of as many as 50 dogs at one time, some of them temporary guests and others unwanted dogs once slated for euthanasia. The Cesar Millan Foundation’s website describes the Santa Clarita center as a 43-acre facility that rehabilitates dogs, but it does not specify how many are housed there, so the figure of 50 comes from a biographical reference and not from an independent count.How the Cesar Millan Foundation frames the anti-euthanasia missionThe website of the foundation claims that its mission is to ensure that none of the dogs is starving, gets sick, or is euthanized. The Cesar Millan Foundation describes the Dog Psychology Center as a ranch-like environment where dogs can recover, learn, and thrive. This is what the foundation claims as its mission statement, and there is no other source verifying these claims independently. There are no statistics on the number of rehabilitated or adopted dogs currently available.What the available records establish about the Dog PsychologyThe records reviewed establish a limited picture. The center moved from South Los Angeles to a 43-acre location in Santa Clarita, a move the sources date to 2007 or 2009. Newsmakers says the center keeps a revolving pack of as many as 50 dogs, some of them unwanted dogs once slated for euthanasia, while the foundation states an anti-euthanasia mission that no independent source verifies.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Arizona teen gave an elderly stranger his shoes, learnt he had lost his wife, then launched a GoFundMe that raised $25,000
articles.summary: An act of kindness outside a pharmacy in Maricopa, Arizona, turned into a community effort to support an elderly man grieving the loss of his wife.
articles.body: An act of kindness outside a pharmacy in Maricopa, Arizona, turned into a community effort to support an elderly man grieving the loss of his wife. Jordan Hope, an 18-year-old, gave his shoes to a stranger whose footwear was falling apart. During their conversation, Hope learnt that the man, known publicly as Mr Roy, had lost his wife about two weeks earlier. He went on to buy him candy, arrange lunch, help him get home and stay in touch by phone. Hope later launched a GoFundMe campaign to help cover Mr Roy’s essential expenses, and the fundraiser raised around $25,000.Arizona teen's act of kindness began with a pair of shoesHope was driving to a bank to deposit money when he noticed Mr Roy outside a Walgreens near John Wayne Parkway and Smith-Enke Road in Maricopa. The older man’s shoes were badly worn and barely stayed on his feet, prompting Hope to give him the shoes he was wearing. A bystander, Yareli Madrid, recorded the encounter and shared the video on Facebook. Hope initially drove away but later returned and found Mr Roy inside the store trying to buy candy, which he paid for. During their conversation, Hope learnt that the man had lost his wife about two weeks earlier. He offered to take Mr Roy to Culver’s for lunch, but the older man’s swollen legs made it difficult for him to get into Hope’s car. Hope arranged a rideshare, met him at the restaurant, picked up the food and followed him home. He stayed to talk and subsequently began checking on Mr Roy by phone, believing the older man needed a friend during a difficult period.GoFundMe campaign raises $25,000 for Mr RoyHope launched a GoFundMe campaign titled Care for Mr. Roy in His Time of Need on October 7 to help cover groceries, medicines, transportation and other essential expenses. The fundraiser gained attention after the video of the encounter circulated online, attracting donations from people moved by the story. It eventually raised approximately $25,000, according to the updated fundraising figure provided for this article. Hope said he intended to surprise Mr Roy with the money collected. The campaign extended the support beyond the initial encounter, allowing donors to contribute towards the older man’s everyday needs as he dealt with bereavement. What began with a pair of shoes thus grew into a wider effort to help him manage practical expenses during a challenging time.Why Jordan Hope decided to helpHope, a recent high-school graduate, runs a computer-building business serving Maricopa and Casa Grande. He has attributed his decision to help to his Christian faith, his parents and his youth pastor. According to local reporting, he had no idea the encounter had been filmed and learnt about the video after his grandmother shared it in the family group chat the following day. The attention brought his actions to a wider audience, but the encounter itself began without a planned publicity campaign. Hope’s response developed as he learnt more about Mr Roy’s circumstances, turning a brief meeting into continued contact and a fundraising effort.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Anduril CEO Brian Schimpf on Palmer Luckey's company getting multi-billion dollar contracts from the US government; says: I am a lifelong Democrat and have great relationships with ...
articles.summary: Anduril Industries CEO Brian Schimpf has defended the defence technology company's growing list of multi-billion-dollar US government contracts amid
articles.body: Anduril Industries CEO Brian Schimpf has defended the defence technology company's growing list of multi-billion-dollar US government contracts amid scrutiny over co-founder Palmer Luckey's close ties to the Trump administration, saying the company has enjoyed strong growth under leaders from both political parties. Speaking to CNBC's Squawk on the Street, Schimpf pushed back against suggestions that Luckey's political connections have helped Anduril secure lucrative Pentagon deals. "We've done incredibly well under [President Joe] Biden," Schimpf said. "That was one of the biggest ramps that we've had as a company. I'm a lifelong Dem and have great relationships on both sides of the aisle of this."The comments come as Anduril faces increased scrutiny after winning major defence contracts while Luckey takes on a more prominent role in US defence policy circles. On October 6, the company announced a US Navy shipyard contract worth up to $2.9 billion, just days after Luckey was named to the Pentagon's Project Meridian initiative. Earlier this year, Anduril also secured a multi-year Department of Defense contract valued at up to $20 billion.Billions in contractsOn October 6, Anduril announced a shipyard contract with the Navy worth up to $2.9 billion. The award came days after Luckey was named to a Department of Defense group known as Project Meridian. In March, the company also won a multi-year Pentagon contract worth up to $20 billion. The appointments of Luckey and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to the initiative have prompted concerns over whether executives whose companies receive billions in federal contracts should have an active role in shaping defense strategy.Schimpf rejected the suggestion that political connections influence awards. “The reality is that the [Department of Defense] has just an incredibly structured process for how they evaluate all these incoming bids,” he said. “So everything goes through these very competitive processes, and we win based on the merits.”Political donationsMusk has given more than $276 million to Republican groups since July, CNBC reported this week. Luckey, who helped raise money for Donald Trump’s 2020 campaign, has donated more than $500,000 to Republican candidates and GOP-aligned groups this year, according to a CNBC analysis of Federal Election Commission filings.$90 billion tender offerSeparately, Anduril this week opened a tender offer to employees in 16 countries that would value the company at $90 billion, five months after it topped a $60 billion valuation. Schimpf said the structure lets Anduril offer employees liquidity without the distraction of stock price swings. Like Anthropic, OpenAI and Databricks, Anduril has benefited from abundant private market funding, which has allowed companies to delay going public.Luckey has said he intends to eventually take the California-based company public. Schimpf told CNBC in July that Anduril is not rushing into an IPO, noting that a hype cycle is “a bad time” to debut. “This allows us to stay really focused on what we need to do, which is a massive, unprecedented ramp in defense production that we need to execute on over the next couple of years,” Schimpf said of the tender offer.AI and the use of forceFounded in 2017 to challenge traditional defense contractors, Anduril has built a reputation for autonomous unmanned systems, drone boats and software supplied to the U.S. Department of Defense and allied militaries. It is among a growing number of defense startups deploying systems overseas, including in the Middle East, as the U.S. government looks to expand next-generation capabilities.The use of AI-equipped systems has raised ethical questions about human oversight. Anthropic’s recent dispute with the Pentagon stemmed from a disagreement over the use of its models in military conflict.Asked about the issue, Schimpf said that decisions about the use of force ultimately rest with people. “Fundamentally, anytime you are making critical decisions about use of force or how to employ these, or what the consequences are of your actions, that is fundamentally a human decision,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Georgia father signed a deed giving property to his son, then signed another two days later naming his daughter as the recipient; the court upheld the earlier transfer
articles.summary: A Georgia father transferred his property to his son through a signed deed in June 2016, only to sign another deed giving the same property to his
articles.body: A Georgia father transferred his property to his son through a signed deed in June 2016, only to sign another deed giving the same property to his daughter two days later. The competing documents eventually led to a family dispute that reached the Georgia Court of Appeals, where judges upheld the earlier transfer. The June 18, 2026, ruling in Choi v. Choi clarified how an improperly witnessed deed can remain legally binding between the people involved, even when questions arise about its formal registration.Georgia father’s two property deeds to his son and daughterThe dispute concerned a property in Lawrenceville, Gwinnett County, Georgia, and the competing claims of a father’s two children, Abraham Jang Kyong Choi and Kang Hee Choi.According to the Georgia Court of Appeals judgment, the father, Kwan Bok Choi, signed a quitclaim deed transferring his interest in the property to his son on June 25, 2016. The document referred to a payment of one dollar, alongside other valuable considerations.A quitclaim deed is a legal document through which a person transfers whatever ownership interest they hold in a property to another person. The document does not, by itself, guarantee that the person transferring the property has a clear title or that the property is free of other claims.The first deed was witnessed by a notary public and the son, who acted as an unofficial witness. Two days later, on June 27, the father signed a second quitclaim deed purporting to transfer the same property to his daughter. That document referred to consideration of ten dollars and was witnessed by a notary public and an employee of the law firm that helped prepare it.The two deeds created competing claims to the same property. The second document had a different witness arrangement, but the court ultimately focused on the legal effect of the earlier transfer and whether the daughter qualified for protection against her brother’s existing interest.How did the competing property documents become a family disputeThe dispute became more complicated when the father signed his last will and testament on July 22, 2016, leaving the property to his daughter. He died in October that year, leaving 3 documents that appeared to point towards different outcomes: the first deed to his son, the second deed to his daughter and a will naming his daughter as the beneficiary.In July 2022, the son filed a petition seeking a judicial declaration that he was the property's sole owner. His sister challenged that position, arguing that the second deed was valid and the first deed was invalid. She also brought counterclaims alleging interference with her inheritance and expected gift.The trial court heard evidence during a 5-day hearing, including testimony from the siblings and other witnesses. The attorneys involved in preparing the father's will and the second deed also provided evidence.The trial court ruled in favour of the son, declaring him the sole legal owner under the first deed. It cancelled the second deed and established that the will could not change the legal effect of the earlier transfer. The daughter appealed the decision, bringing the dispute before the state's appellate court.What does Georgia law require for a valid property deedThe case turned partly on Section 44-5-30 of the Georgia Code, which establishes the formal requirements for deeds conveying land.According to the Georgia Code provision, a deed must be an original written document signed by the person making the transfer. It must also be attested by an authorised officer and one additional witness, delivered to the purchaser or their representative, and supported by good or valuable consideration.The daughter argued that her father's first deed did not satisfy the witnessing requirements because she believed the son, as the recipient of the property, could not serve as the required unofficial witness.However, the Court of Appeals distinguished between the formal requirements for recording a deed and its validity between the parties involved.The judges explained that a deed that does not meet the prescribed witnessing requirements may be unsuitable for recording and may not provide public notice in the usual way. Nevertheless, earlier Georgia decisions established that a written deed signed by the person transferring the property can remain binding between the parties and their heirs, even if it has not been properly witnessed or recorded.The court relied on these established legal principles in assessing the daughter's challenge.Why did the daughter lose her claim to the propertyAnother important consideration was whether the daughter could claim protection as a bona fide purchaser for value. In property law, this generally refers to someone who acquires property in good faith, provides valuable consideration and meets the applicable requirements for protection against earlier interests.The appellate judgment noted that the daughter did not argue that she qualified for this protection. The evidence also indicated that the second transfer was intended as a gift rather than a conventional purchase.The court considered the family relationship, the small amount of consideration stated in the second deed and the daughter's own affidavit describing the property as a gift from her father. She had not demonstrated that she paid additional consideration for the house.Consequently, the daughter could not rely on the protections available to a qualifying purchaser to defeat her brother's earlier interest. The court held that the first deed remained valid against the father and his heirs, including his daughter.On June 18, 2026, the Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court's judgment. The decision did not establish that every improperly witnessed deed is automatically enforceable in every situation. Instead, it confirmed that the specific defect raised in this case did not invalidate the transfer between the father and son.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pakistan to chair IMF, World Bank boards in 2027; first time in over 70 years
articles.summary: Pakistan will take over the chairmanship of the boards of governors of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in 2027, returning to the
articles.body: Pakistan will take over the chairmanship of the boards of governors of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in 2027, returning to the position for the first time since 1953, the country’s ministry of economic affairs said on Friday.The announcement was made during the plenary session of the 2026 WBG-IMF annual meetings in Bangkok, where Pakistan’s minister for economic affairs Ahad Khan Cheema, who also serves as the country’s governor to the World Bank, was formally designated as the incoming chair, PTI reported.Describing the appointment as a “historic milestone”, the ministry said the role would allow Pakistan to participate in shaping global economic and development discussions and encourage constructive engagement among member countries.The annual meetings, scheduled from October 12 to 18, have brought together more than 15,000 participants representing 191 countries.The appointment comes as Pakistan continues to rely on financial assistance from the IMF through two programmes: a USD 7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and a USD 1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).While the EFF is aimed at meeting the country’s balance-of-payments needs and supporting economic reforms, the RSF provides longer-term funding to help Pakistan tackle climate-related risks and improve its resilience.Pakistan could receive a further USD 1.2 billion from the IMF, subject to approval by the fund’s Executive Board. The anticipated disbursement follows an agreement reached between IMF staff and Pakistani authorities on the latest reviews of both programmes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: NEW DLEHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was taken into preventive detention shortly after leaving the residence where he was staying
articles.body: NEW DLEHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was taken into preventive detention shortly after leaving the residence where he was staying to attend the 'Tiranga Yatra' at Delhi's Connaught Place (CP).As Dipke left the residence of NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande, a police official told him, "We are placing you under preventive detention. Section 163 is in force in Connaught Place. You are being detained."Section 163 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) restricts gatherings or specific activities in a designated area."I'm alone, what law did I break," Dipke asked before he was detained.Meanwhile, Rajeev Ranjan, additional CP, Delhi Police PRO said: "I would like to clarify that no one has approached us regarding this matter. We have not received any communication or request concerning a specific list of individuals...The Flag Code has been officially notified and mandates that the national flag must be hoisted with the utmost respect. All the rules stipulated in the Flag Code have been notified and are available in the public domain. In fact, just a short while ago, we shared a post on social media outlining the precautions that every Indian citizen should take when hoisting the national flag."He also criticised those selectively sharing photographs or videos of police officers performing their duties, calling it "entirely inappropriate and illegal"."Sharing the personal information of any police officer—or, for that matter, any individual—on social media in this manner is a clear violation of their privacy. It has come to our notice that certain social media accounts are selectively sharing photographs or videos of police officers performing their duties, along with their personal information. This is entirely inappropriate and illegal," Rajeev Ranjan said.According to officials, a notice issued on behalf of the New Delhi district authorities under the Delhi Police Act directed people not to visit Central Park, citing the restrictions in force under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).A second notice was issued to Dipke by the South West Delhi authorities, reminding him that he, along with CJP co-conveners Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, had previously been 'bound down' (placed under a legal undertaking) after their preventive detention at the airport and subsequent production before a court.The court had directed them to refrain from causing any public disturbance for a period of one year.Earlier today, Dipke defended the party's protests, asserting that peaceful demonstrations were a democratic right. articles.title: Katie Zacharia admits she failed the bar exam on her first attempt in 2011, years after calling herself a lawyer
articles.summary: The new White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia, admitted that she failed her bar exam the first time she took it in 2011 in California and never
articles.body: The new White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia, admitted that she failed her bar exam the first time she took it in 2011 in California and never retook it, as she then moved to China with her husband. In an interview on Fox News with Sean Hannity, Zacharia said she was told that she could call herself a lawyer but not an attorney and that's what she did throughout, but some social media posts called her attorney. "I graduated Pepperdine, got married in the same week, and we had all intent to move out to China," she explained. "I had already preregistered for the bar exam and... during the summer, I knew I would be living in China and the results of the bar were inconsequential, and I sat for it because I didn't wanna have a withdrawal status.""When I went to go engage in media and give legal analysis, I consulted attorneys and legal professionals as to whether or not they agreed that I could be labeled a lawyer, both because I had a valid Juris Doctor from a good law school, a reputable law school, Pepperdine Law School, and in conjunction with the fact that I did have actual substantive legal experience," Zacharia said, setting the record straight.She said she never took the exams because she did not intend to practise law with four kids. She worked at a Chinese law firm as an advisor and that role did not require her to pass the bar exam, she said.On doing a 'bad job' on first dayZacharia said she had very little prep time for her first press conference. "What I feel is I really stepped up to the plate to do the press conference," she told host Sean Hannity. "With very little prep time, I received briefing materials in the morning of Tuesday.""Given the fact that I'd been on the job less than maybe eight hours and had a briefing book in the morning, I feel like I did my very best, Sean, to deliver for the American people that day," Zacharia said."I took several questions and I think it's been mixed because they've said I only took questions from conservative outlets. However, the Daily Mail is not known to be a conservative outlet or friendly to conservatives, so I do challenge that narrative.""I was able to deliver breaking news, which I do believe was the right thing to do as the press secretary," she said, referring to the breaking news that the DonaldTrump administration asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign from her post as the ambassador to Greece.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW Delhi: The ministry of external affairs on Friday expressed concern over the foiled mass-shooting plot targeting a Hindu temple in Aurora, near Chicago."This is obviously a matter of deep concern for us. At the same time it is something that shows or highlights the increasing cases of hate crimes and racial discrimination against the Indian communities in the United States," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal during bi-weekly media briefing."We have taken note of the action that the US law enforcement authorities have undertaken once this incident happened but we call on the United States side to ensure the safety, security and security of the Indian nationals in the country," he added.This comes after a 19-year-old man, Alexandros Paporakis, has been charged with making a terrorist threat and unlawful possession of a weapon after allegedly threatening a mass shooting at the Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Temple in Aurora, near Chicago. articles.title: MEA confirms Jaishankar-Rubio talks in Mumbai after Rahul’s jibe over India visit
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday confirmed that external affairs minister S Jaishankar will hold talks with US secretary of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday confirmed that external affairs minister S Jaishankar will hold talks with US secretary of state Marco Rubio on October 20, while also hosting UAE deputy prime minister and foreign minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Mumbai on October 19 and 20.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal announced the engagements while responding to a question from news agency ANI about whether Jaishankar was expected to hold any meetings in Mumbai next week.“So on October 19 and 20, the external affairs minister will host in Mumbai the deputy prime minister and foreign minister of UAE, Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, for an official visit, on 20th October, external affairs minister will hold talks with the US secretary of state Marco Rubio and attend the celebration of the 250th anniversary of the independence of the United States of America as the guest of honor,” Jaiswal said.ALSO READ: ‘Ensure safety of Indian nationals’: MEA’s strong message to US after alleged Hindu temple attack plotHe also explained that hosting foreign dignitaries outside the national capital was not unusual, pointing to previous engagements held in different Indian cities.“This has been the practice for the last decade or so that we have hosted foreign secretaries outside Delhi. The Prime Minister hosted the Prime Minister of Spain in Baroda. He hosted chancellor Merz in Ahmedabad. Prime Minister of Mauritius was hosted by him in Varanasi, and then the external affairs minister hosted the foreign ministers Meeting in Goa. He hosted the foreign minister of Botswana in Kevadia in Gujarat, and the external affairs minister also hosted the Heart of Asia Conference in Amritsar,” Jaiswal said.Rahul's jibe at govt over Rubio’s visitThe clarification comes after Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi over Rubio’s upcoming visit to Mumbai, alleging that officials in the external affairs ministry were unclear about the developments.“Mr Rubio has summoned his employee to Mumbai. Modi ji, your officials in the external affairs ministry are confused about what's going on. You might want to explain. Unless, of course, you want me to,” Rahul posted on X on Friday.His remarks followed criticism from Congress a day earlier, after US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said American officials expected Jaishankar to meet Rubio in Mumbai. The party questioned why the Indian government had not publicly announced the minister’s engagements.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh had described the ambassador’s statement as “extraordinary” and questioned why details of Jaishankar’s planned meeting with Rubio were being communicated by a US official rather than India’s foreign ministry.“Why is the MEA silent on the external affairs minister's tryst with Mr Rubio in Mumbai?” Ramesh asked, adding that India was learning about the developments from the US ambassador.The US state department announced on Tuesday that Rubio would visit India from October 17 to 22 to strengthen energy cooperation. His itinerary includes Mumbai and Jamnagar, following a visit to Samarkand in Uzbekistan.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Kiran Kaur, mother of murderer Vickrum Digwa, might be released early under new UK sentencing laws, raising concerns for Henry Nowak's family. The case highlights significant changes in the justice system and ongoing appeals for both Kaur and Digwa.
articles.body: The mother of a Sikh man jailed for murdering an 18-year-old student Henry Nowak could leave prison early under changes to England’s early release rules.Kiran Kaur, 53, was sentenced to three years in prison in July for removing the knife her son, Vickrum Digwa, used to kill Nowak in Southampton in December. Kaur is appealing against her sentence, with her case due before the Court of Appeal on November 5.Donna Jones, Hampshire and Isle of Wight’s Police and Crime Commissioner, said an early release would be a significant setback for Nowak’s family.“She wasn't even sentenced until July this year, which was just three months ago, and here we are now talking about her potential release,” Jones told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme.Jones said she would write to Justice Secretary Alex Norris to seek clarification on the rules so she could continue supporting the family.The changes were introduced under the Sentencing Act 2026, which came into force on October 1. Under the new system, most prisoners serving fixed-term sentences of up to two and a half years are automatically released on licence after serving one-third of their sentence, rather than half.Kaur’s offence, assisting an offender, is not among those excluded from the revised scheme. She would serve the remainder of her sentence in the community under licence conditions and could be returned to prison if she breached them.The Ministry of Justice said the 221 days Kaur spent on remand had been taken into account when she was sentenced. It remains unclear whether she could also face deportation.The government said it would “always seek to deport foreign criminals at the first opportunity”. Foreign nationals sentenced to 12 months or more in prison are generally considered for deportation, although exceptions apply and decisions can be appealed.The Ministry of Justice said new licence measures include a presumption that prison leavers will be electronically tagged, restrictions confining some offenders to agreed areas, and allowing victims to have a say in licence conditions. Near real-time location data for probation officers is due to be rolled out nationally by the end of 2026.A government spokesperson said: “Our thoughts remain with the family and friends of Henry Nowak, whose life was cruelly cut short in a horrific act of violence.”Digwa was sentenced to life imprisonment on June 1, with a minimum term of 21 years, for killing Nowak after falsely claiming the student had racially abused him. He has also been granted permission to challenge the length of his sentence at the Court of Appeal on November 5.Kaur was jailed for removing the murder weapon and hiding it at the family home, where police later found it among more than 20 other weapons. Prosecutor Nicholas Lobbenberg described her role in concealing the knife as “crucial” and called her actions “criminality of the highest order”.Sentencing her in July, Judge William Mousley KC said Kaur had acted to protect her son rather than for personal gain, but said she still had to be punished for her actions and to deter others from doing the same.You use AI every day.
